content:
To merge (squash) the last two commits into one:

```bash
git rebase -i HEAD~2
```

An editor will open showing something like:

```text
pick abc1234 First commit
pick def5678 Second commit
```

Change the second `pick` to `squash` (or `s`):

```text
pick abc1234 First commit
squash def5678 Second commit
```

Save and close the editor.

Git will then open another editor to let you edit the combined commit message. Save and close it.

That’s it — the last two commits are now one commit.

If the commits were already pushed, you’ll need to force-push:

```bash
git push --force-with-lease
```

Use `--force-with-lease` instead of `--force` because it is safer.
